chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who made a vow for Allah upon himself and did not specify it, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he specified it, then it is that which he specified, and if he did not specify it, then there is nothing upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person makes a vow to Allah but does not specify what the vow entails?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the juristic principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) is applied to vows: since the obligation is contingent on specification, the default state remains non-obligatory until the vow-maker explicitly defines the act. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on clarity in religious commitments, distinguishing between conditional vows and absolute ones, and ensures that believers are not burdened by ambiguous self-imposed duties.
